ko.title: [농업 101 #8] 당신의 마트 토마토가 존재하는 이유: 품종 개량이라고 불리는 10,000년 엔지니어링 프로젝트

segments.src: > Every crop you eat is a designed product — the result of centuries of choosing which plants get to become parents.
segments.tr: > 당신이 먹는 모든 작물은 설계된 제품입니다 — 어떤 식물이 부모가 될지 선택하는 수백 년간의 결과입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Plant breeding is, at its core, controlled parenthood for crops.
segments.tr: 품종 개량은 근본적으로 작물에 대한 통제된 번식입니다.

segments.src: A breeder decides which two plants mate, then decides which of their offspring get to reproduce again.
segments.tr: 육종가는 어떤 두 식물이 교배할지 결정한 후, 자손 중 누가 다시 번식할지 결정합니다.

segments.src: Repeat for a decade or two, and you have a new variety — what farmers call a *cultivar*.
segments.tr: 이를 10년 또는 20년간 반복하면 새로운 품종을 얻게 됩니다 — 농부들이 *품종*이라고 부르는 것입니다.

segments.src: There are two classic tools in the kit.
segments.tr: 도구함에는 두 가지 고전적인 도구가 있습니다.

segments.src: **Selection breeding** is the older and simpler one.
segments.tr: **선발 육종**이 더 오래되고 더 단순한 방법입니다.

segments.src: You plant a field, walk through it, and keep seed only from the plants you like — the ones that resisted the blight, ripened early, or didn't fall over in a storm.
segments.tr: 당신은 밭에 씨를 뿌리고, 그 안을 돌아다니며, 마음에 드는 식물들에서만 씨앗을 채취합니다 — 병해에 저항한 것들, 빨리 익은 것들, 폭풍에 넘어지지 않은 것들 말입니다.

segments.src: You're not creating anything new; you're concentrating the good genes that already exist in the population.
segments.tr: 당신은 새로운 것을 만들고 있는 것이 아닙니다. 이미 집단에 존재하는 좋은 유전자들을 농축하고 있을 뿐입니다.

segments.src: This is how humans turned a scraggly Mexican grass called teosinte into corn, one selective harvest at a time.
segments.tr: 이렇게 해서 인간은 멕시코의 티오신테라는 까다로운 풀을 옥수수로 바꾸었습니다. 한 번의 선택적 수확씩 말입니다.

segments.src: **Cross breeding (hybridization)** is more deliberate.
segments.tr: **교배 육종(잡종화)**은 더 의도적입니다.

segments.src: You take two parents with different strengths — say, a wheat line with excellent bread-making quality and another that shrugs off stem rust — and physically move pollen from one to the other.
segments.tr: 당신은 서로 다른 강점을 가진 두 부모를 선택합니다 — 예를 들어, 훌륭한 제빵 품질을 가진 밀 계통과 줄기 녹병에 저항하는 계통을 선택한 후 한쪽에서 다른 쪽으로 꽃가루를 물리적으로 옮깁니다.

segments.src: The first generation of offspring is a genetic shuffle.
segments.tr: 첫 번째 세대 자손은 유전적 섞임입니다.

segments.src: Then the real work begins: growing out thousands of descendants and selecting, generation after generation, for the rare individual that inherited both traits at once.
segments.tr: 그 다음부터 진정한 작업이 시작됩니다: 수천 개의 자손을 키우면서 세대를 거쳐 두 특성을 모두 물려받은 드문 개체를 찾아내는 것입니다.

segments.src: Why so slow?
segments.tr: 왜 이렇게 오래 걸릴까요?

segments.src: Because traits come bundled.
segments.tr: 특성이 묶여 있기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Genes sit on chromosomes like beads on a string, and neighboring genes tend to travel together — a phenomenon called **linkage**.
segments.tr: 유전자는 끈 위의 구슬처럼 염색체 위에 앉아 있으며, 이웃한 유전자들은 함께 이동하는 경향이 있습니다 — 이것을 **연관**이라는 현상이라고 합니다.

segments.src: The disease resistance you want may be shackled to a gene for lousy flavor.
segments.tr: 원하는 질병 저항성이 형편없는 맛을 위한 유전자와 함께 묶여 있을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Breaking that link takes many generations of crossing and screening.
segments.tr: 그 연관을 끊으려면 많은 세대에 걸친 교배와 선발이 필요합니다.

segments.src: A new apple variety typically takes 15 to 25 years from first cross to supermarket shelf.
segments.tr: 새로운 사과 품종은 일반적으로 첫 교배부터 슈퍼마켓 진열대까지 15년에서 25년이 걸립니다.

segments.src: Corn hybrids move faster, roughly 7 to 10 years.
segments.tr: 옥수수 교배종은 더 빠르게 진행되며, 대략 7년에서 10년입니다.

segments.src: There's also a trick breeders discovered around 1900 and commercialized in the 1930s: **hybrid vigor** (heterosis).
segments.tr: 1900년경에 육종가들이 발견하고 1930년대에 상용화한 수법도 있습니다: **교배종 활력**(이형접합성).

segments.src: Cross two very inbred, weak-looking parent lines, and the offspring often outperform *both* parents dramatically.
segments.tr: 매우 근친교배되고 약해 보이는 두 부모 계통을 교배하면, 자손은 종종 *두* 부모 모두를 극적으로 능가합니다.

segments.src: Nobody fully understood the mechanism at first — they just knew it worked, and it roughly doubled U.S.
segments.tr: 처음에는 아무도 그 메커니즘을 완전히 이해하지 못했습니다 — 단지 그것이 작동한다는 것을 알고 있었고, 미국의

segments.src: corn yields over a few decades.
segments.tr: 옥수수 수확량을 수십 년에 걸쳐 대략 두 배로 늘렸습니다.

segments.src: The catch: hybrid vigor doesn't carry into the next generation, which is why farmers buy fresh hybrid seed each year rather than saving their own.
segments.tr: 문제는: 교배종 활력이 다음 세대로 이어지지 않으므로, 농부들은 자신의 씨앗을 저장하지 않고 매년 새로운 교배종 씨앗을 구입합니다.

segments.src: Now the uncomfortable part.
segments.tr: 이제 불편한 부분입니다.

segments.src: Every round of selection *throws genes away*.
segments.tr: 선발의 모든 라운드는 *유전자를 버립니다*.

segments.src: That's the whole point — you're narrowing the population toward an ideal.
segments.tr: 그것이 바로 요점입니다 — 당신은 집단을 이상적인 것으로 좁혀나가고 있습니다.

segments.src: But narrow far enough and the entire crop becomes genetically uniform, which means a single new pathogen can hit every field simultaneously.
segments.tr: 하지만 충분히 좁혀지면 전체 작물이 유전적으로 균일해져서, 단일한 새로운 병원체가 모든 밭을 동시에 타격할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Ireland's 1840s potato famine happened partly because the potatoes grown there descended from a tiny founding sample, and *Phytophthora infestans* found no genetic variation to slow it down.
segments.tr: 1840년대 아일랜드의 감자 기근은 부분적으로 거기서 재배된 감자가 작은 창립 표본에서 내려왔고, *감자역병균*이 그것을 늦출 유전적 변이를 찾지 못했기 때문에 발생했습니다.

segments.src: In 1970, Southern corn leaf blight destroyed roughly 15% of the U.S.
segments.tr: 1970년에 남부 옥수수 잎마름병이 미국의

segments.src: corn crop because a shared bit of cytoplasm — used to simplify hybrid seed production — turned out to be a shared vulnerability.
segments.tr: 옥수수 작물의 약 15%를 파괴했습니다. 교배종 씨앗 생산을 간소화하기 위해 사용된 세포질의 공유 부분이 공유 취약점이 되었기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Which brings us to **germplasm conservation**: the deliberate stockpiling of genetic diversity that current varieties don't need but future ones might.
segments.tr: 이는 우리를 **종질 보존**으로 이끕니다: 현재 품종이 필요로 하지 않지만 미래 품종이 필요할 수 있는 유전적 다양성의 의도적 축적입니다.

segments.src: Seed banks store hundreds of thousands of accessions — landraces, wild relatives, obsolete varieties — at around -18°C.
segments.tr: 종자은행은 약 -18°C에서 수십만 개의 유지본(재래종, 야생 친척, 구식 품종)을 저장합니다.

segments.src: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway is the famous backup-of-backups, holding duplicate samples from gene banks worldwide inside a mountain in the Arctic.
segments.tr: 노르웨이의 스발바르 글로벌 종자 금고는 유명한 백업의 백업이며, 북극의 산 속에 세계 유전자은행의 중복 표본을 보유하고 있습니다.

segments.src: The USDA runs its own national system, including the National Laboratory for Genetic Resources Preservation in Fort Collins, Colorado.
segments.tr: 미국 농무부는 콜로라도 포트콜린스의 국가 유전자원 보존 연구실을 포함하여 자체 국가 시스템을 운영합니다.

segments.src: Some crops — potatoes, bananas, apples — can't be stored as dried seed at all and must be kept as living plants in field orchards or as tissue cultures in vitro, which is far more expensive and fragile.
segments.tr: 감자, 바나나, 사과 같은 일부 작물은 건조 씨앗으로 저장할 수 없으며, 들판 과수원의 살아있는 식물이나 시험관 내 조직 배양으로 유지되어야 합니다. 이는 훨씬 더 비싸고 취약합니다.

segments.src: The economics are stark.
segments.tr: 경제학은 명확합니다.

segments.src: Breeding programs are slow, capital-intensive, and their payoff arrives long after the person who started them has retired.
segments.tr: 육종 프로그램은 느리고 자본 집약적이며, 그들의 이득은 그들을 시작한 사람이 은퇴한 지 오래 후에 나타납니다.

segments.src: Yet the raw material — a wild grass on a hillside in Turkey, a farmer's heirloom bean in Peru — is essentially free until it's gone forever.
segments.tr: 그러나 원료 재료 — 터키 언덕의 야생 풀, 페루 농부의 전승 콩 — 는 본질적으로 영원히 없어질 때까지 무료입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활에서

segments.src: Walk into any American supermarket in winter and pick up a tomato.
segments.tr: 겨울에 미국의 어느 슈퍼마켓이든 들어가 토마토를 집어듭니다.

segments.src: It's firm, uniformly red, and tastes like nothing in particular.
segments.tr: 그것은 단단하고, 균일하게 빨간색이며, 특별히 어떤 맛도 나지 않습니다.

segments.src: That's not an accident or a conspiracy — it's a selection outcome.
segments.tr: 그것은 우연이나 음모가 아닙니다 — 선발의 결과입니다.

segments.src: Starting in the 1950s, tomato breeders selected hard for a trait called *uniform ripening*: fruit that turns red evenly from shoulder to blossom end, making it easy for pickers and machines to judge harvest timing.
segments.tr: 1950년대부터 토마토 육종가들은 *균일한 익음*이라는 특성을 강하게 선발했습니다: 어깨에서 꽃 끝까지 균일하게 빨간색으로 변하는 과일로, 수확자와 기계가 수확 시기를 판단하기 쉽게 합니다.

segments.src: It worked beautifully.
segments.tr: 그것은 아름답게 작동했습니다.

segments.src: Growers loved it, and it became near-universal in commercial fresh-market tomatoes.
segments.tr: 재배자들은 그것을 좋아했고, 상업용 신선 시장 토마토에서 거의 보편적이 되었습니다.

segments.src: Then in 2012, a research team at UC Davis and Cornell identified the gene behind uniform ripening — and found the mutation had a hidden cost.
segments.tr: 그러면 2012년에 UC Davis와 Cornell의 연구팀이 균일한 익음 뒤의 유전자를 식별했습니다 — 그리고 그 돌연변이가 숨겨진 비용을 가지고 있었다는 것을 발견했습니다.

segments.src: The normal version of that gene helps drive chloroplast development in the developing fruit, which in turn feeds sugar and aroma compound production.
segments.tr: 그 유전자의 정상 버전은 발달하는 과일의 엽록체 발달을 촉진하는 데 도움을 주며, 이는 당과 향 화합물 생산을 공급합니다.

segments.src: The uniform-ripening mutation switches it partly off.
segments.tr: 균일한 익음 돌연변이는 그것을 부분적으로 끕니다.

segments.src: Breeders had spent 60 years unknowingly selecting for slightly less sugar and flavor.
segments.tr: 육종가들은 60년 동안 의도치 않게 조금 더 적은 설탕과 맛을 선발했습니다.

segments.src: Linkage and hidden trade-offs, exactly as described above.
segments.tr: 연관과 숨겨진 트레이드오프, 정확히 위에서 설명한 대로입니다.

segments.src: Meanwhile, the heirloom tomatoes at your farmers market — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — are essentially unimproved varieties that farmers stopped selecting for shipping traits.
segments.tr: 한편, 당신의 농부 시장의 전승 토마토들 — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — 은 본질적으로 농부들이 배송 특성을 위해 선발하기를 멈춘 개선되지 않은 품종입니다.

segments.src: They taste better and bruise if you look at them funny.
segments.tr: 그들은 더 맛있고 이상하게 보면 멍이 듭니다.

segments.src: At $4 to $6 per pound versus roughly $2 for standard supermarket tomatoes, you're paying for the traits breeders traded away, plus the shipping losses.
segments.tr: 표준 슈퍼마켓 토마토의 약 $2에 비해 파운드당 $4에서 $6에서, 당신은 육종가들이 거래한 특성과 배송 손실을 위해 돈을 지불하고 있습니다.

segments.src: The story has a follow-up worth noting.
segments.tr: 이 이야기는 주목할 만한 후속 조치가 있습니다.

segments.src: Once breeders knew the flavor gene existed, they could go back into germplasm collections, find wild and heirloom lines carrying the functional version, and begin crossing it back in.
segments.tr: 일단 육종가들이 맛 유전자가 존재한다는 것을 알게 되면, 종질 수집으로 돌아가서 기능 버전을 운반하는 야생 및 전승 계통을 찾아서 그것을 다시 교배하기 시작할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Several improved-flavor commercial tomatoes released since have drawn on exactly that approach.
segments.tr: 그 이후로 출시된 여러 개선된 맛의 상업용 토마토들은 정확히 그 접근 방식을 따랐습니다.

segments.src: The genetic material was still available only because somebody had bothered to preserve varieties nobody was growing.
segments.tr: 유전 물질은 누군가 아무도 재배하지 않는 품종을 보존하기 위해 신경을 썼기 때문에만 여전히 이용 가능했습니다.

segments.src: Same logic explains the apple aisle.
segments.tr: 같은 논리가 사과 코너를 설명합니다.

segments.src: Red Delicious dominated American orchards for decades because it shipped and stored well and looked spectacular — while its eating quality steadily declined as growers selected ever-redder, thicker-skinned sports.
segments.tr: Red Delicious는 배송과 저장이 잘 되고 멋있어 보였기 때문에 미국의 과수원에서 수십 년 동안 지배했습니다 — 한편 재배자들이 점점 더 빨간색, 더 두꺼운 피부의 변종을 선발하면서 그 식용 품질은 꾸준히 감소했습니다.

segments.src: Honeycrisp, released by the University of Minnesota in 1991 after a breeding program begun in the 1960s, was selected primarily for the crisp texture consumers actually wanted.
segments.tr: 미네소타 대학에서 1991년에 출시한 Honeycrisp는 1960년대에 시작된 육종 프로그램 이후 소비자들이 실제로 원하는 바삭한 식감을 위해 주로 선발되었습니다.

segments.src: It now commands a substantial price premium.
segments.tr: 그것은 이제 상당한 가격 프리미엄을 누립니다.

segments.src: That's roughly 30 years of publicly funded breeding embodied in a single apple.
segments.tr: 그것은 단일 사과에 구현된 약 30년의 공공 자금 육종입니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Selection breeding concentrates good genes already in a population; cross breeding combines strengths from different parents, then spends 10 to 25 years untangling the traits that came bundled with them.
segments.tr: 1. 선발 육종은 이미 집단에 있는 좋은 유전자를 농축합니다. 교배 육종은 서로 다른 부모의 강점을 결합한 다음 그들과 함께 온 특성을 풀기 위해 10년에서 25년을 소비합니다.

segments.src: 2. Every improvement narrows genetic diversity, and uniform crops are uniformly vulnerable — as the 1970 U.S. corn blight and the Irish potato famine both demonstrated.
segments.tr: 2. 모든 개선은 유전적 다양성을 좁히고, 균일한 작물은 균일하게 취약합니다 — 1970년 미국의 옥수수 마름병과 아일랜드 감자 기근이 모두 보여주었습니다.

segments.src: 3. Seed banks and germplasm collections preserve the genes today's varieties don't need, because the fix for tomorrow's problem usually already exists in some plant nobody is currently growing.
segments.tr: 3. 종자은행과 종질 수집은 오늘날의 품종이 필요로 하지 않는 유전자를 보존합니다. 왜냐하면 내일의 문제에 대한 해결책은 보통 현재 아무도 재배하지 않는 어떤 식물에 이미 존재하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 진단 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A farmer plants a field, saves seed only from the plants that survived a drought, and repeats for several years.
segments.tr: **1.** 농부는 밭을 심고, 가뭄을 견딘 식물들의 씨앗만 저장하고, 몇 년 동안 반복합니다.

segments.src: This is primarily an example of:
segments.tr: 이는 주로 다음의 예입니다:

segments.src: - (a) Cross breeding
segments.tr: - (a) 교배 육종

segments.src: - (b) Selection breeding
segments.tr: - (b) 선발 육종

segments.src: - (c) Hybrid vigor
segments.tr: - (c) 교배종 활력

segments.src: - (d) Germplasm conservation
segments.tr: - (d) 종질 보존

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Farmers who plant hybrid corn can save seed from their harvest and expect the same yield performance the following year.
segments.tr: **2.** 참 또는 거짓: 교배종 옥수수를 심는 농부들은 수확에서 씨앗을 저장하고 다음 해에 같은 수확량 성능을 기대할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **3.** Why do seed banks preserve old, low-yielding, and wild crop varieties that no farmer wants to grow?
segments.tr: **3.** 종자은행이 아무 농부도 재배하고 싶어 하지 않는 오래되고, 저산량의, 야생 작물 품종을 보존하는 이유는 무엇입니까?

segments.src: - (a) They usually outyield modern varieties under good conditions
segments.tr: - (a) 그들은 보통 좋은 조건에서 현대 품종을 능가합니다.

segments.src: - (b) Legal requirements prohibit destroying any plant variety
segments.tr: - (b) 법적 요구사항이 어떤 식물 품종도 파괴하는 것을 금지합니다.

segments.src: - (c) They may carry genes — for disease resistance, flavor, or stress tolerance — needed by future breeding programs
segments.tr: - (c) 그들은 미래의 육종 프로그램이 필요로 하는 질병 저항성, 맛, 또는 스트레스 내성을 위한 유전자를 운반할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - (d) They are cheaper to store than modern varieties
segments.tr: - (d) 그들은 현대 품종보다 저장하기가 더 저렴합니다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Cultivar** — A cultivated variety with distinct, stable traits, maintained through deliberate propagation (e.g., Honeycrisp, Brandywine).
segments.tr: - **품종(Cultivar)** — 의도적 번식을 통해 유지되는 명확하고 안정적인 특성을 가진 재배 품종입니다(예: Honeycrisp, Brandywine).

segments.src: - **Selection breeding** — Improving a crop by repeatedly saving seed only from the best-performing individuals in a population.
segments.tr: - **선발 육종** — 집단에서 최고 성능의 개인으로부터만 반복해서 씨앗을 저장하여 작물을 개선합니다.

segments.src: - **Cross breeding (hybridization)** — Deliberately mating two different parent lines to combine their desirable traits in the offspring.
segments.tr: - **교배 육종(잡종화)** — 두 개의 다른 부모 계통을 의도적으로 교배하여 자손의 바람직한 특성을 결합합니다.

segments.src: - **Hybrid vigor (heterosis)** — The tendency of offspring from two inbred lines to outperform both parents; it does not persist into the following generation.
segments.tr: - **교배종 활력(이형접합성)** — 두 개의 근친교배 계통의 자손이 두 부모 모두를 능가하는 경향입니다. 다음 세대로 지속되지 않습니다.

segments.src: - **Linkage** — The tendency of genes located near each other on the same chromosome to be inherited together, which makes separating good traits from bad ones slow work.
segments.tr: - **연관** — 같은 염색체에서 서로 가까운 위치에 있는 유전자들이 함께 유전되는 경향입니다. 이는 좋은 특성을 나쁜 특성으로부터 분리하기를 느린 작업으로 만듭니다.

segments.src: - **Germplasm** — The living genetic material (seeds, tissue, whole plants) that carries a crop's hereditary information and serves as the raw material for breeding.
segments.tr: - **종질(Germplasm)** — 작물의 유전 정보를 운반하고 육종의 원료로 작용하는 살아있는 유전 물질(씨앗, 조직, 전체 식물)입니다.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (b).** No controlled mating is happening; the farmer is simply concentrating drought-tolerance genes already present in the population.
segments.tr: *답: **1 — (b).** 통제된 교배가 일어나지 않습니다. 농부는 단순히 이미 집단에 존재하는 가뭄 내성 유전자를 농축하고 있습니다.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Hybrid vigor is strongest in the first generation and breaks down afterward as the offspring segregate, which is why hybrid seed is repurchased annually.
segments.tr: **2 — 거짓.** 교배종 활력은 첫 번째 세대에서 가장 강하고 자손이 분리되면서 그 후로 붕괴됩니다. 이것이 교배종 씨앗이 매년 재구입되는 이유입니다.

segments.src: **3 — (c).** Their present-day agronomic performance is beside the point; their value is as a genetic reservoir.
segments.tr: **3 — (c).** 그들의 현재 농학적 성능은 핵심과 상관없습니다. 그들의 가치는 유전적 저수지로서입니다.

segments.src: The 2012 tomato flavor-gene discovery is a concrete case — the functional gene version was recoverable only because heirloom and wild lines had been preserved.*
segments.tr: 2012년 토마토 맛 유전자 발견은 구체적인 사례입니다 — 기능 유전자 버전은 전승 및 야생 계통이 보존되었기 때문에만 회수할 수 있었습니다.*

zh.title: [农业101 #8] 你的超市番茄为何存在：被称为植物育种的10,000年工程项目

segments.src: > Every crop you eat is a designed product — the result of centuries of choosing which plants get to become parents.
segments.tr: > 你吃的每种作物都是设计产品——选择哪些植物成为亲本数百年来的结果。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Plant breeding is, at its core, controlled parenthood for crops.
segments.tr: 植物育种的本质是对作物繁殖的人为控制。

segments.src: A breeder decides which two plants mate, then decides which of their offspring get to reproduce again.
segments.tr: 育种者决定哪两株植物交配，然后决定它们的哪些后代再次繁殖。

segments.src: Repeat for a decade or two, and you have a new variety — what farmers call a *cultivar*.
segments.tr: 重复十年或二十年，你就获得了一个新品种——农民称之为*栽培品种*。

segments.src: There are two classic tools in the kit.
segments.tr: 这个领域有两个经典工具。

segments.src: **Selection breeding** is the older and simpler one.
segments.tr: **选择育种**是较老的那个，也较简单。

segments.src: You plant a field, walk through it, and keep seed only from the plants you like — the ones that resisted the blight, ripened early, or didn't fall over in a storm.
segments.tr: 你种下一块田，走过去，只从你喜欢的植物上保留种子——那些抵抗了枯萎病、早熟或在暴风雨中没有倒伏的。

segments.src: You're not creating anything new; you're concentrating the good genes that already exist in the population.
segments.tr: 你没有创造任何新东西；你在浓缩已经存在于种群中的良好基因。

segments.src: This is how humans turned a scraggly Mexican grass called teosinte into corn, one selective harvest at a time.
segments.tr: 这就是人类通过一次次精心选择收获，把一种叫teosinte的杂乱墨西哥草变成玉米的过程。

segments.src: **Cross breeding (hybridization)** is more deliberate.
segments.tr: **杂交育种（人工杂交）**更具有针对性。

segments.src: You take two parents with different strengths — say, a wheat line with excellent bread-making quality and another that shrugs off stem rust — and physically move pollen from one to the other.
segments.tr: 你选择两个具有不同优势的亲本——比如说，一条小麦品系具有优秀的烤焙品质，另一条能抵抗秆锈病——并将花粉从一个转移到另一个。

segments.src: The first generation of offspring is a genetic shuffle.
segments.tr: 第一代后代是一次遗传洗牌。

segments.src: Then the real work begins: growing out thousands of descendants and selecting, generation after generation, for the rare individual that inherited both traits at once.
segments.tr: 然后真正的工作开始了：培育数千个后代，一代又一代地选择，寻找同时继承两种性状的罕见个体。

segments.src: Why so slow?
segments.tr: 为什么这么慢？

segments.src: Because traits come bundled.
segments.tr: 因为性状是捆绑在一起的。

segments.src: Genes sit on chromosomes like beads on a string, and neighboring genes tend to travel together — a phenomenon called **linkage**.
segments.tr: 基因坐在染色体上就像绳子上的珠子一样，相邻基因倾向于一起传递——这种现象称为**连锁**。

segments.src: The disease resistance you want may be shackled to a gene for lousy flavor.
segments.tr: 你想要的抗病性可能被束缚到一个不良风味基因上。

segments.src: Breaking that link takes many generations of crossing and screening.
segments.tr: 打破这种联系需要许多代的杂交和筛选。

segments.src: A new apple variety typically takes 15 to 25 years from first cross to supermarket shelf.
segments.tr: 一个新的苹果品种通常需要15到25年才能从第一次杂交进入超市货架。

segments.src: Corn hybrids move faster, roughly 7 to 10 years.
segments.tr: 玉米杂交种发展更快，大约7到10年。

segments.src: There's also a trick breeders discovered around 1900 and commercialized in the 1930s: **hybrid vigor** (heterosis).
segments.tr: 还有一个育种者在1900年左右发现并在1930年代进行商业化的技巧：**杂交优势**（heterosis）。

segments.src: Cross two very inbred, weak-looking parent lines, and the offspring often outperform *both* parents dramatically.
segments.tr: 杂交两条进行了深度近亲繁殖、看似虚弱的亲本品系，后代通常会显著优于*两个*亲本。

segments.src: Nobody fully understood the mechanism at first — they just knew it worked, and it roughly doubled U.S.
segments.tr: 起初没人完全理解其机制——他们只知道它有效，而且它大约翻倍了美国的

segments.src: corn yields over a few decades.
segments.tr: 玉米产量在几十年间。

segments.src: The catch: hybrid vigor doesn't carry into the next generation, which is why farmers buy fresh hybrid seed each year rather than saving their own.
segments.tr: 问题所在：杂交优势不会延续到下一代，这就是为什么农民每年购买新鲜杂交种子而不是自己保存。

segments.src: Now the uncomfortable part.
segments.tr: 现在来到了不太舒服的部分。

segments.src: Every round of selection *throws genes away*.
segments.tr: 每一轮选择都会*丢弃基因*。

segments.src: That's the whole point — you're narrowing the population toward an ideal.
segments.tr: 那就是全部要点——你在将种群向理想状态缩小。

segments.src: But narrow far enough and the entire crop becomes genetically uniform, which means a single new pathogen can hit every field simultaneously.
segments.tr: 但是如果缩小得足够远，整个作物就变得遗传上一致，这意味着单个新病原体可以同时袭击每个田地。

segments.src: Ireland's 1840s potato famine happened partly because the potatoes grown there descended from a tiny founding sample, and *Phytophthora infestans* found no genetic variation to slow it down.
segments.tr: 爱尔兰1840年代的土豆饥荒部分是因为那里种植的土豆来自一个很小的创始群体，而*Phytophthora infestans*没有遇到任何遗传多样性来减缓其传播。

segments.src: In 1970, Southern corn leaf blight destroyed roughly 15% of the U.S.
segments.tr: 在1970年，玉米南叶枯病摧毁了美国大约15%的

segments.src: corn crop because a shared bit of cytoplasm — used to simplify hybrid seed production — turned out to be a shared vulnerability.
segments.tr: 玉米作物，因为一个共有的细胞质片段——被用来简化杂交种子生产——结果上是一个共有的易感性。

segments.src: Which brings us to **germplasm conservation**: the deliberate stockpiling of genetic diversity that current varieties don't need but future ones might.
segments.tr: 这把我们带到**种质保存**：有意储备当前品种不需要但未来品种可能需要的遗传多样性。

segments.src: Seed banks store hundreds of thousands of accessions — landraces, wild relatives, obsolete varieties — at around -18°C.
segments.tr: 种子库储存数十万份种质资源——地方品种、野生亲缘、已废止品种——在大约-18°C。

segments.src: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway is the famous backup-of-backups, holding duplicate samples from gene banks worldwide inside a mountain in the Arctic.
segments.tr: 挪威的斯瓦尔巴全球种子库是著名的'备份的备份'，在北极一座山内保存来自世界各地基因库的重复样本。

segments.src: The USDA runs its own national system, including the National Laboratory for Genetic Resources Preservation in Fort Collins, Colorado.
segments.tr: 美国农业部运营其国家系统，包括位于科罗拉多州Fort Collins的国家遗传资源保护实验室。

segments.src: Some crops — potatoes, bananas, apples — can't be stored as dried seed at all and must be kept as living plants in field orchards or as tissue cultures in vitro, which is far more expensive and fragile.
segments.tr: 一些作物——土豆、香蕉、苹果——根本无法作为干燥种子保存，必须作为活植物保存在田间果园中或作为体外组织培养物，这远更昂贵且脆弱。

segments.src: The economics are stark.
segments.tr: 经济形势是严峻的。

segments.src: Breeding programs are slow, capital-intensive, and their payoff arrives long after the person who started them has retired.
segments.tr: 育种项目进展缓慢、资本密集，而且收益出现在项目启动者早已退休之后。

segments.src: Yet the raw material — a wild grass on a hillside in Turkey, a farmer's heirloom bean in Peru — is essentially free until it's gone forever.
segments.tr: 然而原始材料——土耳其山坡上的野生草，秘鲁农民的世传豆——本质上是免费的，直到它永远消失。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Walk into any American supermarket in winter and pick up a tomato.
segments.tr: 在冬天走进任何美国超市，拿起一个番茄。

segments.src: It's firm, uniformly red, and tastes like nothing in particular.
segments.tr: 它很硬、色泽均匀的红色、味道平凡无奇。

segments.src: That's not an accident or a conspiracy — it's a selection outcome.
segments.tr: 那不是巧合或阴谋——那是选择的结果。

segments.src: Starting in the 1950s, tomato breeders selected hard for a trait called *uniform ripening*: fruit that turns red evenly from shoulder to blossom end, making it easy for pickers and machines to judge harvest timing.
segments.tr: 从1950年代开始，番茄育种者为了一种叫*均匀成熟*的性状进行强力选择：果实从肩部到蕊端均匀变红，方便采摘者和机械判断收获时间。

segments.src: It worked beautifully.
segments.tr: 这招非常有效。

segments.src: Growers loved it, and it became near-universal in commercial fresh-market tomatoes.
segments.tr: 种植者喜欢它，而且它在商业鲜食番茄中几乎成为通用标准。

segments.src: Then in 2012, a research team at UC Davis and Cornell identified the gene behind uniform ripening — and found the mutation had a hidden cost.
segments.tr: 然后在2012年，UC Davis和康奈尔大学的研究团队确定了均匀成熟背后的基因——并发现这个突变有一个隐藏的代价。

segments.src: The normal version of that gene helps drive chloroplast development in the developing fruit, which in turn feeds sugar and aroma compound production.
segments.tr: 该基因的正常版本有助于促进发育果实中的叶绿体发育，进而促进糖和芳香化合物的产生。

segments.src: The uniform-ripening mutation switches it partly off.
segments.tr: 均匀成熟突变将其部分关闭。

segments.src: Breeders had spent 60 years unknowingly selecting for slightly less sugar and flavor.
segments.tr: 育种者在不知情的情况下花了60年时间选择了更低的糖含量和风味。

segments.src: Linkage and hidden trade-offs, exactly as described above.
segments.tr: 连锁和隐藏的折衷，正如上面所述的那样。

segments.src: Meanwhile, the heirloom tomatoes at your farmers market — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — are essentially unimproved varieties that farmers stopped selecting for shipping traits.
segments.tr: 同时，你的农贸市场上的传家番茄——Brandywine、Cherokee Purple、Green Zebra——本质上是农民停止刻意选择运输特性的未改良品种。

segments.src: They taste better and bruise if you look at them funny.
segments.tr: 它们味道很好，但一碰就容易受伤。

segments.src: At $4 to $6 per pound versus roughly $2 for standard supermarket tomatoes, you're paying for the traits breeders traded away, plus the shipping losses.
segments.tr: 每磅$4到$6相比标准超市番茄的$2左右，你付的钱实际上是为了育种者曾经舍弃的性状和运输中的损失。

segments.src: The story has a follow-up worth noting.
segments.tr: 这个故事有一个值得注意的后续。

segments.src: Once breeders knew the flavor gene existed, they could go back into germplasm collections, find wild and heirloom lines carrying the functional version, and begin crossing it back in.
segments.tr: 一旦育种者知道风味基因存在，他们就可以回到种质资源库中，寻找携带功能版本的野生和传家品系，并开始将其杂交引入。

segments.src: Several improved-flavor commercial tomatoes released since have drawn on exactly that approach.
segments.tr: 随后发布的几款改良风味商业番茄品种都采用了这种方法。

segments.src: The genetic material was still available only because somebody had bothered to preserve varieties nobody was growing.
segments.tr: 这些遗传材料之所以仍然可用，仅仅是因为有人费力保存了当时没人种植的品种。

segments.src: Same logic explains the apple aisle.
segments.tr: 同样的逻辑也适用于苹果的故事。

segments.src: Red Delicious dominated American orchards for decades because it shipped and stored well and looked spectacular — while its eating quality steadily declined as growers selected ever-redder, thicker-skinned sports.
segments.tr: 'Red Delicious'在美国果园中流行了数十年，因为它易于运输、易于储存、外观极具吸引力——但它的食用品质随着种植者选择越来越红、果皮更厚的变异而不断下降。

segments.src: Honeycrisp, released by the University of Minnesota in 1991 after a breeding program begun in the 1960s, was selected primarily for the crisp texture consumers actually wanted.
segments.tr: 'Honeycrisp'由明尼苏达大学在1991年发布，是一项始于1960年代的育种项目的成果，主要是为了实现消费者真正想要的脆爽口感。

segments.src: It now commands a substantial price premium.
segments.tr: 它现在能获得相当可观的价格溢价。

segments.src: That's roughly 30 years of publicly funded breeding embodied in a single apple.
segments.tr: 这代表了大约30年的公共资助育种工作。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行摘要

segments.src: 1. Selection breeding concentrates good genes already in a population; cross breeding combines strengths from different parents, then spends 10 to 25 years untangling the traits that came bundled with them.
segments.tr: 1. 选择育种是集中种群中已有的良好基因；杂交育种将不同亲本的优势结合，然后需要花10到25年来分离那些与所需性状同时遗传的不利性状。

segments.src: 2. Every improvement narrows genetic diversity, and uniform crops are uniformly vulnerable — as the 1970 U.S. corn blight and the Irish potato famine both demonstrated.
segments.tr: 2. 每项改进都会缩小遗传多样性，统一的作物会统一易受伤害——正如1970年的美国玉米花叶病和爱尔兰土豆大饥荒所证明的。

segments.src: 3. Seed banks and germplasm collections preserve the genes today's varieties don't need, because the fix for tomorrow's problem usually already exists in some plant nobody is currently growing.
segments.tr: 3. 种子库和种质资源库保存了当今品种不需要的基因，因为明天问题的解决方案通常已经存在于某种目前没有人种植的植物中。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测

segments.src: **1.** A farmer plants a field, saves seed only from the plants that survived a drought, and repeats for several years.
segments.tr: **1.** 一位农民种植一片田地，只从抵抗干旱的植物中保存种子，并连续多年重复此过程。

segments.src: This is primarily an example of:
segments.tr: 这主要是以下哪种情况的例子：

segments.src: - (a) Cross breeding
segments.tr: - (a) 杂交育种

segments.src: - (b) Selection breeding
segments.tr: - (b) 选择育种

segments.src: - (c) Hybrid vigor
segments.tr: - (c) 杂交优势

segments.src: - (d) Germplasm conservation
segments.tr: - (d) 种质保存

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Farmers who plant hybrid corn can save seed from their harvest and expect the same yield performance the following year.
segments.tr: **2.** 真假：种植杂交玉米的农民可以从收获中保存种子，并期望第二年获得相同的产量表现。

segments.src: **3.** Why do seed banks preserve old, low-yielding, and wild crop varieties that no farmer wants to grow?
segments.tr: **3.** 为什么种子库保存没有农民想种植的旧的、低产量的和野生作物品种？

segments.src: - (a) They usually outyield modern varieties under good conditions
segments.tr: - (a) 在良好条件下，它们通常比现代品种产量更高

segments.src: - (b) Legal requirements prohibit destroying any plant variety
segments.tr: - (b) 法律要求禁止销毁任何植物品种

segments.src: - (c) They may carry genes — for disease resistance, flavor, or stress tolerance — needed by future breeding programs
segments.tr: - (c) 它们可能携带将来育种项目所需的基因——用于抗病性、风味或抗逆性

segments.src: - (d) They are cheaper to store than modern varieties
segments.tr: - (d) 它们比现代品种更便宜存储

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日词汇

segments.src: - **Cultivar** — A cultivated variety with distinct, stable traits, maintained through deliberate propagation (e.g., Honeycrisp, Brandywine).
segments.tr: - **栽培品种** — 通过有意繁殖维持的、具有鲜明稳定性状的植物品种（如Honeycrisp、Brandywine）。

segments.src: - **Selection breeding** — Improving a crop by repeatedly saving seed only from the best-performing individuals in a population.
segments.tr: - **选择育种** — 通过连续从种群中表现最佳的个体保存种子来改进作物的方法。

segments.src: - **Cross breeding (hybridization)** — Deliberately mating two different parent lines to combine their desirable traits in the offspring.
segments.tr: - **杂交育种** — 有意让两条不同的亲本品系交配，以在后代中结合它们所需的性状。

segments.src: - **Hybrid vigor (heterosis)** — The tendency of offspring from two inbred lines to outperform both parents; it does not persist into the following generation.
segments.tr: - **杂交优势** — 来自两个近交系的后代往往超越两个亲本的现象；这种优势不会延续到下一代。

segments.src: - **Linkage** — The tendency of genes located near each other on the same chromosome to be inherited together, which makes separating good traits from bad ones slow work.
segments.tr: - **连锁** — 同一染色体上靠近的基因一起遗传的趋势，这使得将有利性状与不利性状分离变得缓慢困难。

segments.src: - **Germplasm** — The living genetic material (seeds, tissue, whole plants) that carries a crop's hereditary information and serves as the raw material for breeding.
segments.tr: - **种质** — 携带作物遗传信息并作为育种原料的活的遗传材料（种子、组织、整个植物）。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (b).** No controlled mating is happening; the farmer is simply concentrating drought-tolerance genes already present in the population.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 — (b).** 没有受控的交配发生；农民只是浓缩了已经存在于种群中的抗旱基因。

segments.src: **2 — False.** Hybrid vigor is strongest in the first generation and breaks down afterward as the offspring segregate, which is why hybrid seed is repurchased annually.
segments.tr: **2 — 错误。** 杂交优势在第一代最强，之后随着后代分离而减弱，这就是为什么杂交种子每年都需要重新购买。

segments.src: **3 — (c).** Their present-day agronomic performance is beside the point; their value is as a genetic reservoir.
segments.tr: **3 — (c).** 它们目前的农艺表现无关紧要；它们的价值在于作为遗传资源库。

segments.src: The 2012 tomato flavor-gene discovery is a concrete case — the functional gene version was recoverable only because heirloom and wild lines had been preserved.*
segments.tr: 2012年番茄风味基因的发现就是一个具体案例——功能基因版本之所以可用，完全是因为传家品种和野生品系被保存了下来。*

hi.title: [Agriculture 101 #8] आपके किराना स्टोर के टमाटर का अस्तित्व क्यों है: 10,000-वर्षीय इंजीनियरिंग परियोजना जिसे पौधों का प्रजनन कहा जाता है

segments.src: > Every crop you eat is a designed product — the result of centuries of choosing which plants get to become parents.
segments.tr: > आप जो हर फसल खाते हैं वह एक डिज़ाइन की गई उत्पाद है — यह सदियों तक यह चुनने का परिणाम है कि कौन से पौधे माता-पिता बन जाते हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Plant breeding is, at its core, controlled parenthood for crops.
segments.tr: पौधों का प्रजनन, मूल रूप से, फसलों के लिए नियंत्रित माता-पिता है।

segments.src: A breeder decides which two plants mate, then decides which of their offspring get to reproduce again.
segments.tr: एक प्रजनक यह तय करता है कि कौन से दो पौधे संभोग करते हैं, फिर यह तय करता है कि उनकी संतानों में से कौन फिर से प्रजनन करते हैं।

segments.src: Repeat for a decade or two, and you have a new variety — what farmers call a *cultivar*.
segments.tr: एक या दो दशक के लिए दोहराएं, और आपके पास एक नई किस्म है — जिसे किसान *cultivar* कहते हैं।

segments.src: There are two classic tools in the kit.
segments.tr: किट में दो क्लासिक उपकरण हैं।

segments.src: **Selection breeding** is the older and simpler one.
segments.tr: **चयन प्रजनन** पुराना और सरल है।

segments.src: You plant a field, walk through it, and keep seed only from the plants you like — the ones that resisted the blight, ripened early, or didn't fall over in a storm.
segments.tr: आप एक खेत में पौधे लगाते हैं, इसके माध्यम से चलते हैं, और केवल उन पौधों से बीज रखते हैं जो आपको पसंद हैं — जो सड़न का विरोध करते हैं, जल्दी पकते हैं, या तूफान में नहीं गिरते।

segments.src: You're not creating anything new; you're concentrating the good genes that already exist in the population.
segments.tr: आप कुछ नया नहीं बना रहे हैं; आप अच्छे जीन को केंद्रित कर रहे हैं जो आबादी में पहले से मौजूद हैं।

segments.src: This is how humans turned a scraggly Mexican grass called teosinte into corn, one selective harvest at a time.
segments.tr: इसी तरह मनुष्य ने teosinte नामक एक खुरदुरी मैक्सिकन घास को मकई में बदल दिया, एक बार में एक चयनात्मक कटाई।

segments.src: **Cross breeding (hybridization)** is more deliberate.
segments.tr: **क्रॉस प्रजनन (संकरण)** अधिक जानबूझकर है।

segments.src: You take two parents with different strengths — say, a wheat line with excellent bread-making quality and another that shrugs off stem rust — and physically move pollen from one to the other.
segments.tr: आप विभिन्न ताकत वाले दो माता-पिता लेते हैं — कहते हैं, उत्कृष्ट रोटी-निर्माण गुणवत्ता वाली गेहूँ की रेखा और एक जो तने की जंग को दूर करता है — और भौतिक रूप से एक से दूसरे में पराग स्थानांतरित करते हैं।

segments.src: The first generation of offspring is a genetic shuffle.
segments.tr: संतानों की पहली पीढ़ी एक आनुवंशिक फेरबदल है।

segments.src: Then the real work begins: growing out thousands of descendants and selecting, generation after generation, for the rare individual that inherited both traits at once.
segments.tr: फिर असली काम शुरू होता है: हजारों वंशजों को विकसित करना और पीढ़ी दर पीढ़ी चुनना, उस दुर्लभ व्यक्ति के लिए जिसने एक बार में दोनों लक्षण विरासत में लिए हों।

segments.src: Why so slow?
segments.tr: यह बहुत धीमा क्यों है?

segments.src: Because traits come bundled.
segments.tr: क्योंकि लक्षण बंडल में आते हैं।

segments.src: Genes sit on chromosomes like beads on a string, and neighboring genes tend to travel together — a phenomenon called **linkage**.
segments.tr: जीन गुणसूत्रों पर मनके की तरह बैठते हैं, और पड़ोसी जीन एक साथ यात्रा करते हैं — एक घटना जिसे **संबंध** कहा जाता है।

segments.src: The disease resistance you want may be shackled to a gene for lousy flavor.
segments.tr: जिस रोग प्रतिरोध को आप चाहते हैं वह बुरे स्वाद के लिए एक जीन से जुड़ा हो सकता है।

segments.src: Breaking that link takes many generations of crossing and screening.
segments.tr: उस लिंक को तोड़ने में क्रॉसिंग और स्क्रीनिंग की कई पीढ़ियां लगती हैं।

segments.src: A new apple variety typically takes 15 to 25 years from first cross to supermarket shelf.
segments.tr: एक नई सेब की किस्म को आमतौर पर पहली क्रॉसिंग से सुपरमार्केट शेल्फ तक 15 से 25 साल का समय लगता है।

segments.src: Corn hybrids move faster, roughly 7 to 10 years.
segments.tr: मकई संकर तेजी से आगे बढ़ते हैं, लगभग 7 से 10 साल।

segments.src: There's also a trick breeders discovered around 1900 and commercialized in the 1930s: **hybrid vigor** (heterosis).
segments.tr: प्रजनकों द्वारा 1900 के आसपास खोजी गई एक चाल भी है और 1930 के दशक में वाणिज्य किया गया: **संकर शक्ति** (विषमता)।

segments.src: Cross two very inbred, weak-looking parent lines, and the offspring often outperform *both* parents dramatically.
segments.tr: दो बहुत ही अंतर्प्रजनित, कमजोर दिखने वाली माता-पिता की रेखाओं को क्रॉस करें, और संतानें अक्सर *दोनों* माता-पिता को नाटकीय रूप से बेहतर प्रदर्शन करती हैं।

segments.src: Nobody fully understood the mechanism at first — they just knew it worked, and it roughly doubled U.S.
segments.tr: शुरुआत में किसी ने भी तंत्र को पूरी तरह नहीं समझा — वे सिर्फ जानते थे कि यह काम करता है, और इसने यू.एस. को लगभग दोगुना कर दिया।

segments.src: corn yields over a few decades.
segments.tr: मकई की पैदावार कुछ दशकों में।

segments.src: The catch: hybrid vigor doesn't carry into the next generation, which is why farmers buy fresh hybrid seed each year rather than saving their own.
segments.tr: पकड़: संकर शक्ति अगली पीढ़ी में नहीं जाती है, इसलिए किसान अपना बचाने के बजाय हर साल ताजा संकर बीज खरीदते हैं।

segments.src: Now the uncomfortable part.
segments.tr: अब असहज भाग।

segments.src: Every round of selection *throws genes away*.
segments.tr: चयन का हर दौर *जीन को दूर फेंकता है*।

segments.src: That's the whole point — you're narrowing the population toward an ideal.
segments.tr: यही पूरा मुद्दा है — आप आदर्श की ओर जनसंख्या को संकीर्ण कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: But narrow far enough and the entire crop becomes genetically uniform, which means a single new pathogen can hit every field simultaneously.
segments.tr: लेकिन काफी हद तक संकीर्ण करें और पूरी फसल आनुवंशिक रूप से एकसमान हो जाती है, जिसका अर्थ है कि एक भी नया रोगज़नक़ एक साथ हर खेत को मार सकता है।

segments.src: Ireland's 1840s potato famine happened partly because the potatoes grown there descended from a tiny founding sample, and *Phytophthora infestans* found no genetic variation to slow it down.
segments.tr: आयरलैंड के 1840 के दशक की आलू की भुखमरी आंशिक रूप से इसलिए हुई क्योंकि वहां उगाई जाने वाली आलू एक छोटे संस्थापक नमूने से उतरी थी, और *Phytophthora infestans* को इसे धीमा करने के लिए कोई आनुवंशिक भिन्नता नहीं मिली।

segments.src: In 1970, Southern corn leaf blight destroyed roughly 15% of the U.S.
segments.tr: 1970 में, दक्षिणी मकई पत्ती झुलसा ने यू.एस. के लगभग 15% को नष्ट कर दिया।

segments.src: corn crop because a shared bit of cytoplasm — used to simplify hybrid seed production — turned out to be a shared vulnerability.
segments.tr: मकई की फसल क्योंकि साइटोप्लाज्म का एक साझा टुकड़ा — संकर बीज उत्पादन को सरल बनाने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है — एक साझा कमजोरी बन गया।

segments.src: Which brings us to **germplasm conservation**: the deliberate stockpiling of genetic diversity that current varieties don't need but future ones might.
segments.tr: जो हमें **जीन संरक्षण** में लाता है: आनुवंशिक विविधता का जानबूझकर जमाखोरी जिसकी वर्तमान किस्मों को जरूरत नहीं है लेकिन भविष्य की किस्मों को हो सकती है।

segments.src: Seed banks store hundreds of thousands of accessions — landraces, wild relatives, obsolete varieties — at around -18°C.
segments.tr: बीज बैंक सैकड़ों हजारों प्रमाणीकरण संग्रहीत करते हैं — देशज किस्में, जंगली रिश्तेदार, पुरानी किस्में — लगभग -18°C पर।

segments.src: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway is the famous backup-of-backups, holding duplicate samples from gene banks worldwide inside a mountain in the Arctic.
segments.tr: नॉर्वे में Svalbard ग्लोबल सीड वॉल्ट प्रसिद्ध बैकअप-ऑफ-बैकअप है, जो आर्कटिक में एक पर्वत के अंदर दुनिया भर से जीन बैंकों से नकल नमूने रखता है।

segments.src: The USDA runs its own national system, including the National Laboratory for Genetic Resources Preservation in Fort Collins, Colorado.
segments.tr: USDA अपना राष्ट्रीय प्रणाली चलाता है, जिसमें फोर्ट कॉलिंस, कोलोराडो में आनुवंशिक संसाधन संरक्षण राष्ट्रीय प्रयोगशाला शामिल है।

segments.src: Some crops — potatoes, bananas, apples — can't be stored as dried seed at all and must be kept as living plants in field orchards or as tissue cultures in vitro, which is far more expensive and fragile.
segments.tr: कुछ फसलें — आलू, केले, सेब — बिल्कुल सूखे बीज के रूप में संग्रहीत नहीं हो सकती हैं और उन्हें खेत के बागों में जीवित पौधों के रूप में या विट्रो में ऊतक संस्कृतियों के रूप में रखना चाहिए, जो बहुत अधिक महंगा और नाजुक है।

segments.src: The economics are stark.
segments.tr: अर्थशास्त्र कठोर हैं।

segments.src: Breeding programs are slow, capital-intensive, and their payoff arrives long after the person who started them has retired.
segments.tr: प्रजनन कार्यक्रम धीमे, पूंजी-गहन हैं, और उनका लाभ इसके बाद आता है जब जिस व्यक्ति ने उन्हें शुरू किया वह सेवानिवृत्त हो चुका हो।

segments.src: Yet the raw material — a wild grass on a hillside in Turkey, a farmer's heirloom bean in Peru — is essentially free until it's gone forever.
segments.tr: फिर भी कच्चा माल — तुर्की के एक पहाड़ी पर एक जंगली घास, पेरू में एक किसान की विरासत बीन — अनिवार्य रूप से मुक्त है जब तक कि यह हमेशा के लिए चला न जाए।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Walk into any American supermarket in winter and pick up a tomato.
segments.tr: सर्दियों में किसी भी अमेरिकी सुपरमार्केट में जाएं और एक टमाटर उठाएं।

segments.src: It's firm, uniformly red, and tastes like nothing in particular.
segments.tr: यह दृढ़ है, समान रूप से लाल है, और विशेष रूप से कुछ नहीं चखता है।

segments.src: That's not an accident or a conspiracy — it's a selection outcome.
segments.tr: यह कोई दुर्घटना या षड्यंत्र नहीं है — यह एक चयन परिणाम है।

segments.src: Starting in the 1950s, tomato breeders selected hard for a trait called *uniform ripening*: fruit that turns red evenly from shoulder to blossom end, making it easy for pickers and machines to judge harvest timing.
segments.tr: 1950 के दशक से शुरू करते हुए, टमाटर के प्रजनकों ने *समान पकना* नामक एक लक्षण के लिए कठोरता से चुना: फल जो कंधे से फूल के अंत तक समान रूप से लाल हो जाते हैं, जिससे चुनने वाले और मशीनें कटाई समय का न्याय करना आसान हो जाता है।

segments.src: It worked beautifully.
segments.tr: यह सुंदरता से काम करता था।

segments.src: Growers loved it, and it became near-universal in commercial fresh-market tomatoes.
segments.tr: उत्पादकों को यह पसंद आया, और यह व्यावसायिक ताजा-बाजार टमाटरों में लगभग सार्वभौमिक हो गया।

segments.src: Then in 2012, a research team at UC Davis and Cornell identified the gene behind uniform ripening — and found the mutation had a hidden cost.
segments.tr: फिर 2012 में, यूसी डेविस और कॉर्नेल के एक शोध दल ने समान पकने के पीछे जीन की पहचान की — और पाया कि उत्परिवर्तन की एक छिपी हुई लागत थी।

segments.src: The normal version of that gene helps drive chloroplast development in the developing fruit, which in turn feeds sugar and aroma compound production.
segments.tr: उस जीन का सामान्य संस्करण विकासशील फल में क्लोरोप्लास्ट विकास को चलाने में मदद करता है, जो बदले में चीनी और सुगंध यौगिक उत्पादन को खिलाता है।

segments.src: The uniform-ripening mutation switches it partly off.
segments.tr: समान-पकने का उत्परिवर्तन इसे आंशिक रूप से बंद कर देता है।

segments.src: Breeders had spent 60 years unknowingly selecting for slightly less sugar and flavor.
segments.tr: प्रजनकों ने 60 साल तक अनजाने में थोड़ी कम चीनी और स्वाद के लिए चुना।

segments.src: Linkage and hidden trade-offs, exactly as described above.
segments.tr: संबंध और छिपे हुए व्यापार-बंद, ठीक जैसा कि ऊपर वर्णित है।

segments.src: Meanwhile, the heirloom tomatoes at your farmers market — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — are essentially unimproved varieties that farmers stopped selecting for shipping traits.
segments.tr: इस बीच, आपके किसानों के बाजार में विरासत टमाटर — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — अनिवार्य रूप से अनुत्क्रांत किस्में हैं जो किसानों ने शिपिंग लक्षणों के लिए चुनना बंद कर दिया।

segments.src: They taste better and bruise if you look at them funny.
segments.tr: वे बेहतर स्वाद लेते हैं और अगर आप उन्हें मजेदार तरीके से देखते हैं तो चोट लगती है।

segments.src: At $4 to $6 per pound versus roughly $2 for standard supermarket tomatoes, you're paying for the traits breeders traded away, plus the shipping losses.
segments.tr: मानक सुपरमार्केट टमाटरों के लिए लगभग $2 की तुलना में $4 से $6 प्रति पाउंड पर, आप उन लक्षणों के लिए भुगतान कर रहे हैं जिन्हें प्रजनकों ने व्यापार किया, साथ ही शिपिंग नुकसान।

segments.src: The story has a follow-up worth noting.
segments.tr: कहानी का एक फॉलो-अप ध्यान देने योग्य है।

segments.src: Once breeders knew the flavor gene existed, they could go back into germplasm collections, find wild and heirloom lines carrying the functional version, and begin crossing it back in.
segments.tr: एक बार जब प्रजनकों को पता चल गया कि स्वाद जीन मौजूद है, तो वे जीन संग्रह में वापस जा सकते थे, कार्यात्मक संस्करण ले जाने वाली जंगली और विरासत रेखाएं खोज सकते थे, और इसे वापस में क्रॉस करना शुरू कर सकते थे।

segments.src: Several improved-flavor commercial tomatoes released since have drawn on exactly that approach.
segments.tr: तब से जारी किए गए कई सुधारे स्वाद वाले व्यावसायिक टमाटरों ने बिल्कुल उसी दृष्टिकोण पर ध्यान दिया है।

segments.src: The genetic material was still available only because somebody had bothered to preserve varieties nobody was growing.
segments.tr: आनुवंशिक सामग्री अभी भी उपलब्ध थी क्योंकि किसी ने उन किस्मों को संरक्षित करने की परवाह की जो कोई बढ़ नहीं रहा था।

segments.src: Same logic explains the apple aisle.
segments.tr: समान तर्क सेब गलियारे की व्याख्या करता है।

segments.src: Red Delicious dominated American orchards for decades because it shipped and stored well and looked spectacular — while its eating quality steadily declined as growers selected ever-redder, thicker-skinned sports.
segments.tr: Red Delicious दशकों तक अमेरिकी बागों पर हावी रहा क्योंकि यह अच्छी तरह से भेज और संग्रहीत किया गया था और शानदार दिख रहा था — जबकि इसकी खाने की गुणवत्ता में लगातार गिरावट आई क्योंकि उत्पादकों ने कभी-अधिक लाल, मोटी त्वचा वाले खेल को चुना।

segments.src: Honeycrisp, released by the University of Minnesota in 1991 after a breeding program begun in the 1960s, was selected primarily for the crisp texture consumers actually wanted.
segments.tr: Honeycrisp, मिनेसोटा विश्वविद्यालय द्वारा 1991 में 1960 के दशक में शुरू किए गए एक प्रजनन कार्यक्रम के बाद जारी किया गया, मुख्य रूप से कुरकुरी बनावट के लिए चुना गया जो उपभोक्ता वास्तव में चाहते थे।

segments.src: It now commands a substantial price premium.
segments.tr: यह अब एक पर्याप्त मूल्य प्रीमियम की मांग करता है।

segments.src: That's roughly 30 years of publicly funded breeding embodied in a single apple.
segments.tr: यह एक एकल सेब में सार्वजनिक रूप से वित्त पोषित प्रजनन के लगभग 30 साल है।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Selection breeding concentrates good genes already in a population; cross breeding combines strengths from different parents, then spends 10 to 25 years untangling the traits that came bundled with them.
segments.tr: 1. चयन प्रजनन जनसंख्या में पहले से मौजूद अच्छे जीन को केंद्रित करता है; क्रॉस प्रजनन विभिन्न माता-पिता से ताकत को जोड़ता है, फिर उन लक्षणों को अलग करने में 10 से 25 साल तक बिताता है जो उनके साथ बंडल किए गए थे।

segments.src: 2. Every improvement narrows genetic diversity, and uniform crops are uniformly vulnerable — as the 1970 U.S. corn blight and the Irish potato famine both demonstrated.
segments.tr: 2. हर सुधार आनुवंशिक विविधता को संकीर्ण करता है, और समान फसलें समान रूप से असुरक्षित हैं — जैसा कि 1970 के यू.एस. मकई झुलसा और आयरलैंड की आलू की भुखमरी दोनों ने प्रदर्शित किया।

segments.src: 3. Seed banks and germplasm collections preserve the genes today's varieties don't need, because the fix for tomorrow's problem usually already exists in some plant nobody is currently growing.
segments.tr: 3. बीज बैंक और जीन संग्रह आज की किस्मों को जरूरत न होने वाले जीन को संरक्षित करते हैं, क्योंकि कल की समस्या का समाधान आमतौर पर किसी पौधे में पहले से मौजूद होता है जिसे कोई वर्तमान में नहीं उगा रहा है।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्वयं परीक्षा

segments.src: **1.** A farmer plants a field, saves seed only from the plants that survived a drought, and repeats for several years.
segments.tr: **1.** एक किसान एक खेत में पौधे लगाता है, केवल उन पौधों से बीज बचाता है जो सूखे में जीवित रहे, और कई सालों के लिए दोहराता है।

segments.src: This is primarily an example of:
segments.tr: यह मुख्य रूप से इसका एक उदाहरण है:

segments.src: - (a) Cross breeding
segments.tr: - (a) क्रॉस प्रजनन

segments.src: - (b) Selection breeding
segments.tr: - (b) चयन प्रजनन

segments.src: - (c) Hybrid vigor
segments.tr: - (c) संकर शक्ति

segments.src: - (d) Germplasm conservation
segments.tr: - (d) जीन संरक्षण

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Farmers who plant hybrid corn can save seed from their harvest and expect the same yield performance the following year.
segments.tr: **2.** सत्य या असत्य: जो किसान संकर मकई लगाते हैं वे अपनी कटाई से बीज बचा सकते हैं और अगले साल समान उपज प्रदर्शन की अपेक्षा कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: **3.** Why do seed banks preserve old, low-yielding, and wild crop varieties that no farmer wants to grow?
segments.tr: **3.** बीज बैंक पुरानी, कम उपज वाली, और जंगली फसल किस्मों को क्यों संरक्षित करते हैं जिन्हें कोई किसान नहीं उगाना चाहता?

segments.src: - (a) They usually outyield modern varieties under good conditions
segments.tr: - (a) वे आमतौर पर अच्छी परिस्थितियों में आधुनिक किस्मों को पार करते हैं

segments.src: - (b) Legal requirements prohibit destroying any plant variety
segments.tr: - (b) कानूनी आवश्यकताएं किसी भी पौधे की किस्म को नष्ट करने से मना करती हैं

segments.src: - (c) They may carry genes — for disease resistance, flavor, or stress tolerance — needed by future breeding programs
segments.tr: - (c) वे जीन हो सकते हैं — रोग प्रतिरोध, स्वाद, या तनाव सहनशीलता के लिए — भविष्य के प्रजनन कार्यक्रमों की जरूरत है

segments.src: - (d) They are cheaper to store than modern varieties
segments.tr: - (d) वे आधुनिक किस्मों की तुलना में संग्रहीत करने के लिए सस्ता हैं

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Cultivar** — A cultivated variety with distinct, stable traits, maintained through deliberate propagation (e.g., Honeycrisp, Brandywine).
segments.tr: - **Cultivar** — एक खेती की गई किस्म जिसमें विशिष्ट, स्थिर लक्षण हों, जानबूझकर प्रसार के माध्यम से बनाई गई (उदा., Honeycrisp, Brandywine)।

segments.src: - **Selection breeding** — Improving a crop by repeatedly saving seed only from the best-performing individuals in a population.
segments.tr: - **चयन प्रजनन** — एक फसल में सुधार करना जनसंख्या में केवल सर्वोत्तम प्रदर्शन करने वाले व्यक्तियों से बीज को बार-बार बचाकर।

segments.src: - **Cross breeding (hybridization)** — Deliberately mating two different parent lines to combine their desirable traits in the offspring.
segments.tr: - **क्रॉस प्रजनन (संकरण)** — जानबूझकर दो अलग-अलग माता-पिता की रेखाओं को संभोग करना उनके वांछित लक्षणों को संतान में जोड़ने के लिए।

segments.src: - **Hybrid vigor (heterosis)** — The tendency of offspring from two inbred lines to outperform both parents; it does not persist into the following generation.
segments.tr: - **संकर शक्ति (विषमता)** — दो अंतर्प्रजनित रेखाओं से संतान का दोनों माता-पिता को बेहतर प्रदर्शन करने की प्रवृत्ति; यह अगली पीढ़ी में जारी नहीं रहता है।

segments.src: - **Linkage** — The tendency of genes located near each other on the same chromosome to be inherited together, which makes separating good traits from bad ones slow work.
segments.tr: - **संबंध** — एक ही गुणसूत्र पर एक दूसरे के पास स्थित जीन की एक साथ विरासत में लेने की प्रवृत्ति, जो अच्छे लक्षणों को बुरे लोगों से अलग करना धीमा काम बनाता है।

segments.src: - **Germplasm** — The living genetic material (seeds, tissue, whole plants) that carries a crop's hereditary information and serves as the raw material for breeding.
segments.tr: - **जीन द्रव्य** — जीवित आनुवंशिक सामग्री (बीज, ऊतक, पूरे पौधे) जो एक फसल की वंशानुगत जानकारी को ले जाती है और प्रजनन के लिए कच्चे माल के रूप में काम करती है।

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (b).** No controlled mating is happening; the farmer is simply concentrating drought-tolerance genes already present in the population.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1 — (b).** कोई नियंत्रित संभोग नहीं हो रहा है; किसान केवल सूखा-सहनशीलता जीन को केंद्रित कर रहा है जो आबादी में पहले से मौजूद हैं।

segments.src: **2 — False.** Hybrid vigor is strongest in the first generation and breaks down afterward as the offspring segregate, which is why hybrid seed is repurchased annually.
segments.tr: **2 — असत्य।** संकर शक्ति पहली पीढ़ी में सबसे मजबूत है और बाद में संतान के अलग होने के बाद टूट जाती है, यही कारण है कि संकर बीज वार्षिक रूप से फिर से खरीदा जाता है।

segments.src: **3 — (c).** Their present-day agronomic performance is beside the point; their value is as a genetic reservoir.
segments.tr: **3 — (c).** उनका वर्तमान-दिन कृषि संबंधी प्रदर्शन बात के पास है; उनका मूल्य एक आनुवंशिक जलाशय के रूप में है।

segments.src: The 2012 tomato flavor-gene discovery is a concrete case — the functional gene version was recoverable only because heirloom and wild lines had been preserved.*
segments.tr: 2012 के टमाटर स्वाद-जीन की खोज एक ठोस मामला है — कार्यात्मक जीन संस्करण केवल इसलिए पुनः प्राप्त करने योग्य था क्योंकि विरासत और जंगली रेखाओं को संरक्षित किया गया था।*

es.title: [Agricultura 101 #8] Por qué existe tu tomate de supermercado: El proyecto de ingeniería de 10,000 años llamado mejora de plantas

segments.src: > Every crop you eat is a designed product — the result of centuries of choosing which plants get to become parents.
segments.tr: > Todo cultivo que comes es un producto diseñado — el resultado de siglos eligiendo qué plantas se conviertan en padres.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Plant breeding is, at its core, controlled parenthood for crops.
segments.tr: La mejora de plantas es, en esencia, paternidad controlada para cultivos.

segments.src: A breeder decides which two plants mate, then decides which of their offspring get to reproduce again.
segments.tr: Un mejorador decide qué dos plantas se aparean, luego decide cuál de su descendencia puede reproducirse nuevamente.

segments.src: Repeat for a decade or two, and you have a new variety — what farmers call a *cultivar*.
segments.tr: Repite durante una o dos décadas, y tienes una variedad nueva — lo que los granjeros llaman un *cultivar*.

segments.src: There are two classic tools in the kit.
segments.tr: Hay dos herramientas clásicas en el kit.

segments.src: **Selection breeding** is the older and simpler one.
segments.tr: **La mejora por selección** es la más antigua y simple.

segments.src: You plant a field, walk through it, and keep seed only from the plants you like — the ones that resisted the blight, ripened early, or didn't fall over in a storm.
segments.tr: Plantas un campo, caminas por él, y guardas semilla solo de las plantas que te gustan — las que resistieron la plaga, maduraron temprano, o no se cayeron en una tormenta.

segments.src: You're not creating anything new; you're concentrating the good genes that already exist in the population.
segments.tr: No estás creando nada nuevo; estás concentrando los buenos genes que ya existen en la población.

segments.src: This is how humans turned a scraggly Mexican grass called teosinte into corn, one selective harvest at a time.
segments.tr: Así es como los humanos convirtieron una gramínea mexicana desgarbada llamada teosinte en maíz, una cosecha selectiva a la vez.

segments.src: **Cross breeding (hybridization)** is more deliberate.
segments.tr: **El cruzamiento (hibridación)** es más deliberado.

segments.src: You take two parents with different strengths — say, a wheat line with excellent bread-making quality and another that shrugs off stem rust — and physically move pollen from one to the other.
segments.tr: Tomas dos padres con diferentes fortalezas — digamos, una línea de trigo con excelente calidad para hacer pan y otra que rechaza el óxido del tallo — y mueves físicamente el polen de uno al otro.

segments.src: The first generation of offspring is a genetic shuffle.
segments.tr: La primera generación de descendencia es un revoltijo genético.

segments.src: Then the real work begins: growing out thousands of descendants and selecting, generation after generation, for the rare individual that inherited both traits at once.
segments.tr: Luego comienza el trabajo real: cultivar miles de descendientes y seleccionar, generación tras generación, el raro individuo que heredó ambos rasgos a la vez.

segments.src: Why so slow?
segments.tr: ¿Por qué tan lento?

segments.src: Because traits come bundled.
segments.tr: Porque los rasgos vienen agrupados.

segments.src: Genes sit on chromosomes like beads on a string, and neighboring genes tend to travel together — a phenomenon called **linkage**.
segments.tr: Los genes se sientan en cromosomas como cuentas en una cuerda, y los genes vecinos tienden a viajar juntos — un fenómeno llamado **ligamiento**.

segments.src: The disease resistance you want may be shackled to a gene for lousy flavor.
segments.tr: La resistencia a enfermedades que quieres puede estar encadenada a un gen de mal sabor.

segments.src: Breaking that link takes many generations of crossing and screening.
segments.tr: Romper ese enlace requiere muchas generaciones de cruzamiento y selección.

segments.src: A new apple variety typically takes 15 to 25 years from first cross to supermarket shelf.
segments.tr: Una variedad de manzana nueva típicamente toma de 15 a 25 años desde el primer cruzamiento hasta el estante del supermercado.

segments.src: Corn hybrids move faster, roughly 7 to 10 years.
segments.tr: Los híbridos de maíz avanzan más rápido, aproximadamente 7 a 10 años.

segments.src: There's also a trick breeders discovered around 1900 and commercialized in the 1930s: **hybrid vigor** (heterosis).
segments.tr: También hay un truco que los mejoradores descubrieron alrededor de 1900 y comercializaron en la década de 1930: **vigor híbrido** (heterosis).

segments.src: Cross two very inbred, weak-looking parent lines, and the offspring often outperform *both* parents dramatically.
segments.tr: Cruza dos líneas parentales muy endogámicas y de aspecto débil, y la descendencia a menudo supera *a ambos* padres dramáticamente.

segments.src: Nobody fully understood the mechanism at first — they just knew it worked, and it roughly doubled U.S.
segments.tr: Nadie entendió completamente el mecanismo al principio — solo sabían que funcionaba, y aproximadamente duplicó el de EE.UU.

segments.src: corn yields over a few decades.
segments.tr: rendimientos de maíz en algunas décadas.

segments.src: The catch: hybrid vigor doesn't carry into the next generation, which is why farmers buy fresh hybrid seed each year rather than saving their own.
segments.tr: El truco: el vigor híbrido no se lleva a la siguiente generación, por eso los granjeros compran semilla híbrida fresca cada año en lugar de guardar la suya propia.

segments.src: Now the uncomfortable part.
segments.tr: Ahora la parte incómoda.

segments.src: Every round of selection *throws genes away*.
segments.tr: Cada ronda de selección *descarta genes*.

segments.src: That's the whole point — you're narrowing the population toward an ideal.
segments.tr: Ese es el punto completo — estás estrechando la población hacia un ideal.

segments.src: But narrow far enough and the entire crop becomes genetically uniform, which means a single new pathogen can hit every field simultaneously.
segments.tr: Pero estrechate lo suficiente y todo el cultivo se vuelve genéticamente uniforme, lo que significa que un único patógeno nuevo puede afectar cada campo simultáneamente.

segments.src: Ireland's 1840s potato famine happened partly because the potatoes grown there descended from a tiny founding sample, and *Phytophthora infestans* found no genetic variation to slow it down.
segments.tr: La hambruna de la papa en Irlanda en la década de 1840 sucedió en parte porque las papas cultivadas allí descendían de una pequeña muestra fundadora, y *Phytophthora infestans* no encontró variación genética para desacelerarla.

segments.src: In 1970, Southern corn leaf blight destroyed roughly 15% of the U.S.
segments.tr: En 1970, el tizón de la hoja del maíz del sur destruyó aproximadamente el 15% del de EE.UU.

segments.src: corn crop because a shared bit of cytoplasm — used to simplify hybrid seed production — turned out to be a shared vulnerability.
segments.tr: cultivo de maíz porque una porción compartida de citoplasma — utilizada para simplificar la producción de semilla híbrida — resultó ser una vulnerabilidad compartida.

segments.src: Which brings us to **germplasm conservation**: the deliberate stockpiling of genetic diversity that current varieties don't need but future ones might.
segments.tr: Lo que nos lleva a **conservación de germoplasma**: el almacenamiento deliberado de diversidad genética que las variedades actuales no necesitan pero las futuras podrían.

segments.src: Seed banks store hundreds of thousands of accessions — landraces, wild relatives, obsolete varieties — at around -18°C.
segments.tr: Los bancos de semillas almacenan cientos de miles de accesiones — landraces, parientes silvestres, variedades obsoletas — a alrededor de -18°C.

segments.src: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway is the famous backup-of-backups, holding duplicate samples from gene banks worldwide inside a mountain in the Arctic.
segments.tr: La Bóveda Global de Semillas de Svalbard en Noruega es la famosa copia de seguridad de seguridades, sosteniendo muestras duplicadas de bancos de genes mundiales dentro de una montaña en el Ártico.

segments.src: The USDA runs its own national system, including the National Laboratory for Genetic Resources Preservation in Fort Collins, Colorado.
segments.tr: El USDA ejecuta su propio sistema nacional, incluyendo el Laboratorio Nacional para la Preservación de Recursos Genéticos en Fort Collins, Colorado.

segments.src: Some crops — potatoes, bananas, apples — can't be stored as dried seed at all and must be kept as living plants in field orchards or as tissue cultures in vitro, which is far more expensive and fragile.
segments.tr: Algunos cultivos — papas, plátanos, manzanas — no pueden almacenarse como semilla seca en absoluto y deben mantenerse como plantas vivas en huertos de campo o como cultivos de tejidos in vitro, lo cual es mucho más caro y frágil.

segments.src: The economics are stark.
segments.tr: La economía es cruda.

segments.src: Breeding programs are slow, capital-intensive, and their payoff arrives long after the person who started them has retired.
segments.tr: Los programas de mejora son lentos, intensivos en capital, y su ganancia llega mucho después de que la persona que los comenzó se ha jubilado.

segments.src: Yet the raw material — a wild grass on a hillside in Turkey, a farmer's heirloom bean in Peru — is essentially free until it's gone forever.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, la materia prima — un pasto silvestre en una ladera en Turquía, un frijol heirloom de un granjero en Perú — es esencialmente gratis hasta que se desaparece para siempre.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Walk into any American supermarket in winter and pick up a tomato.
segments.tr: Entra en cualquier supermercado estadounidense en invierno y recoge un tomate.

segments.src: It's firm, uniformly red, and tastes like nothing in particular.
segments.tr: Es firme, rojo uniforme, y sabe a nada en particular.

segments.src: That's not an accident or a conspiracy — it's a selection outcome.
segments.tr: Eso no es un accidente ni una conspiración — es un resultado de selección.

segments.src: Starting in the 1950s, tomato breeders selected hard for a trait called *uniform ripening*: fruit that turns red evenly from shoulder to blossom end, making it easy for pickers and machines to judge harvest timing.
segments.tr: Comenzando en la década de 1950, los mejoradores de tomate seleccionaban duramente un rasgo llamado *maduración uniforme*: fruta que se vuelve roja uniformemente desde el hombro hasta el extremo de la flor, facilitando que los recolectores y máquinas juzguen el momento de cosecha.

segments.src: It worked beautifully.
segments.tr: Funcionó hermosamente.

segments.src: Growers loved it, and it became near-universal in commercial fresh-market tomatoes.
segments.tr: A los productores les encantó, y se volvió casi universal en tomates comerciales de mercado fresco.

segments.src: Then in 2012, a research team at UC Davis and Cornell identified the gene behind uniform ripening — and found the mutation had a hidden cost.
segments.tr: Luego en 2012, un equipo de investigación en UC Davis y Cornell identificó el gen detrás de la maduración uniforme — y encontraron que la mutación tenía un costo oculto.

segments.src: The normal version of that gene helps drive chloroplast development in the developing fruit, which in turn feeds sugar and aroma compound production.
segments.tr: La versión normal de ese gen ayuda a impulsar el desarrollo del cloroplasto en la fruta en desarrollo, que a su vez alimenta la producción de azúcar y compuestos de aroma.

segments.src: The uniform-ripening mutation switches it partly off.
segments.tr: La mutación de maduración uniforme lo apaga parcialmente.

segments.src: Breeders had spent 60 years unknowingly selecting for slightly less sugar and flavor.
segments.tr: Los mejoradores habían pasado 60 años seleccionando inconscientemente por un poco menos de azúcar y sabor.

segments.src: Linkage and hidden trade-offs, exactly as described above.
segments.tr: Ligamiento e intercambios ocultos, exactamente como se describe arriba.

segments.src: Meanwhile, the heirloom tomatoes at your farmers market — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — are essentially unimproved varieties that farmers stopped selecting for shipping traits.
segments.tr: Mientras tanto, los tomates heirloom en tu mercado de agricultores — Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Green Zebra — son esencialmente variedades sin mejorar que los granjeros dejaron de seleccionar para rasgos de envío.

segments.src: They taste better and bruise if you look at them funny.
segments.tr: Saben mejor y se magullan si los miras de forma extraña.

segments.src: At $4 to $6 per pound versus roughly $2 for standard supermarket tomatoes, you're paying for the traits breeders traded away, plus the shipping losses.
segments.tr: A $4 a $6 por libra versus aproximadamente $2 para tomates estándar de supermercado, estás pagando por los rasgos que los mejoradores intercambiaron, más las pérdidas de envío.

segments.src: The story has a follow-up worth noting.
segments.tr: La historia tiene un seguimiento digno de nota.

segments.src: Once breeders knew the flavor gene existed, they could go back into germplasm collections, find wild and heirloom lines carrying the functional version, and begin crossing it back in.
segments.tr: Una vez que los mejoradores sabían que el gen de sabor existía, podían volver a las colecciones de germoplasma, encontrar líneas silvestres y heirloom que llevaban la versión funcional, y comenzar a cruzarlas nuevamente.

segments.src: Several improved-flavor commercial tomatoes released since have drawn on exactly that approach.
segments.tr: Varios tomates comerciales de sabor mejorado lanzados desde entonces han tomado exactamente ese enfoque.

segments.src: The genetic material was still available only because somebody had bothered to preserve varieties nobody was growing.
segments.tr: El material genético aún estaba disponible solo porque alguien se había molestado en preservar variedades que nadie estaba cultivando.

segments.src: Same logic explains the apple aisle.
segments.tr: La misma lógica explica el pasillo de manzanas.

segments.src: Red Delicious dominated American orchards for decades because it shipped and stored well and looked spectacular — while its eating quality steadily declined as growers selected ever-redder, thicker-skinned sports.
segments.tr: Red Delicious dominó huertos estadounidenses durante décadas porque se transportaba y almacenaba bien y se veía espectacular — mientras su calidad de consumo disminuía constantemente a medida que los productores seleccionaban deportes cada vez más rojos y de piel más gruesa.

segments.src: Honeycrisp, released by the University of Minnesota in 1991 after a breeding program begun in the 1960s, was selected primarily for the crisp texture consumers actually wanted.
segments.tr: Honeycrisp, lanzada por la Universidad de Minnesota en 1991 después de un programa de mejora comenzado en la década de 1960, fue seleccionada principalmente por la textura crujiente que los consumidores realmente querían.

segments.src: It now commands a substantial price premium.
segments.tr: Ahora ordena una prima de precio sustancial.

segments.src: That's roughly 30 years of publicly funded breeding embodied in a single apple.
segments.tr: Eso es aproximadamente 30 años de mejora financiada públicamente encarnada en una sola manzana.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Selection breeding concentrates good genes already in a population; cross breeding combines strengths from different parents, then spends 10 to 25 years untangling the traits that came bundled with them.
segments.tr: 1. La mejora por selección concentra buenos genes ya en una población; el cruzamiento combina fortalezas de diferentes padres, luego pasa 10 a 25 años desenredando los rasgos que vinieron agrupados con ellos.

segments.src: 2. Every improvement narrows genetic diversity, and uniform crops are uniformly vulnerable — as the 1970 U.S. corn blight and the Irish potato famine both demonstrated.
segments.tr: 2. Cada mejora estrecha la diversidad genética, y los cultivos uniformes son uniformemente vulnerables — como el tizón del maíz estadounidense de 1970 y la hambruna de la papa irlandesa demostraron.

segments.src: 3. Seed banks and germplasm collections preserve the genes today's varieties don't need, because the fix for tomorrow's problem usually already exists in some plant nobody is currently growing.
segments.tr: 3. Los bancos de semillas y colecciones de germoplasma preservan los genes que las variedades actuales no necesitan, porque la solución para el problema de mañana generalmente ya existe en alguna planta que nadie está cultivando actualmente.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **1.** A farmer plants a field, saves seed only from the plants that survived a drought, and repeats for several years.
segments.tr: **1.** Un granjero planta un campo, guarda semilla solo de las plantas que sobrevivieron a una sequía, y repite durante varios años.

segments.src: This is primarily an example of:
segments.tr: Esto es principalmente un ejemplo de:

segments.src: - (a) Cross breeding
segments.tr: - (a) Cruzamiento

segments.src: - (b) Selection breeding
segments.tr: - (b) Mejora por selección

segments.src: - (c) Hybrid vigor
segments.tr: - (c) Vigor híbrido

segments.src: - (d) Germplasm conservation
segments.tr: - (d) Conservación de germoplasma

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Farmers who plant hybrid corn can save seed from their harvest and expect the same yield performance the following year.
segments.tr: **2.** Verdadero o Falso: Los granjeros que plantan maíz híbrido pueden guardar semilla de su cosecha y esperar el mismo desempeño de rendimiento el año siguiente.

segments.src: **3.** Why do seed banks preserve old, low-yielding, and wild crop varieties that no farmer wants to grow?
segments.tr: **3.** ¿Por qué los bancos de semillas preservan variedades de cultivos antiguos, de bajo rendimiento y silvestres que ningún granjero quiere cultivar?

segments.src: - (a) They usually outyield modern varieties under good conditions
segments.tr: - (a) Generalmente superan las variedades modernas bajo buenas condiciones

segments.src: - (b) Legal requirements prohibit destroying any plant variety
segments.tr: - (b) Los requisitos legales prohíben destruir cualquier variedad de planta

segments.src: - (c) They may carry genes — for disease resistance, flavor, or stress tolerance — needed by future breeding programs
segments.tr: - (c) Pueden llevar genes — para resistencia a enfermedades, sabor, o tolerancia al estrés — necesarios por programas de mejora futuros

segments.src: - (d) They are cheaper to store than modern varieties
segments.tr: - (d) Son más baratos de almacenar que las variedades modernas

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Cultivar** — A cultivated variety with distinct, stable traits, maintained through deliberate propagation (e.g., Honeycrisp, Brandywine).
segments.tr: - **Cultivar** — Una variedad cultivada con rasgos distintos y estables, mantenida a través de propagación deliberada (por ej., Honeycrisp, Brandywine).

segments.src: - **Selection breeding** — Improving a crop by repeatedly saving seed only from the best-performing individuals in a population.
segments.tr: - **Mejora por selección** — Mejorar un cultivo guardando repetidamente semilla solo de los individuos de mejor desempeño en una población.

segments.src: - **Cross breeding (hybridization)** — Deliberately mating two different parent lines to combine their desirable traits in the offspring.
segments.tr: - **Cruzamiento (hibridación)** — Aparear deliberadamente dos líneas parentales diferentes para combinar sus rasgos deseables en la descendencia.

segments.src: - **Hybrid vigor (heterosis)** — The tendency of offspring from two inbred lines to outperform both parents; it does not persist into the following generation.
segments.tr: - **Vigor híbrido (heterosis)** — La tendencia de la descendencia de dos líneas endogámicas a superar a ambos padres; no persiste en la siguiente generación.

segments.src: - **Linkage** — The tendency of genes located near each other on the same chromosome to be inherited together, which makes separating good traits from bad ones slow work.
segments.tr: - **Ligamiento** — La tendencia de genes ubicados cerca uno del otro en el mismo cromosoma a ser heredados juntos, lo que hace que separar buenos rasgos de malos sea trabajo lento.

segments.src: - **Germplasm** — The living genetic material (seeds, tissue, whole plants) that carries a crop's hereditary information and serves as the raw material for breeding.
segments.tr: - **Germoplasma** — El material genético vivo (semillas, tejido, plantas completas) que lleva la información hereditaria de un cultivo y sirve como materia prima para la mejora.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (b).** No controlled mating is happening; the farmer is simply concentrating drought-tolerance genes already present in the population.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1 — (b).** No está sucediendo apareamiento controlado; el granjero simplemente está concentrando genes de tolerancia a la sequía ya presentes en la población.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Hybrid vigor is strongest in the first generation and breaks down afterward as the offspring segregate, which is why hybrid seed is repurchased annually.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** El vigor híbrido es más fuerte en la primera generación y se desmorona después a medida que la descendencia se segrega, por eso la semilla híbrida se recompra anualmente.

segments.src: **3 — (c).** Their present-day agronomic performance is beside the point; their value is as a genetic reservoir.
segments.tr: **3 — (c).** Su desempeño agronómico actual no es el punto; su valor es como un reservorio genético.

segments.src: The 2012 tomato flavor-gene discovery is a concrete case — the functional gene version was recoverable only because heirloom and wild lines had been preserved.*
segments.tr: El descubrimiento del gen de sabor del tomate de 2012 es un caso concreto — la versión del gen funcional era recuperable solo porque líneas heirloom y silvestres habían sido preservadas.*

ar.title: [الزراعة 101 #8] لماذا طماطمك في محل البقالة موجودة: مشروع الهندسة التي استغرقت 10,000 سنة يسمى تحسين النباتات

segments.src: > Every crop you eat is a designed product — the result of centuries of choosing which plants get to become parents.
segments.tr: > كل محصول تأكله هو منتج مصمم — نتيجة قرون من اختيار أي النباتات تصبح آباء.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Plant breeding is, at its core, controlled parenthood for crops.
segments.tr: تحسين النباتات هو، في جوهره، الأبوة المراقبة للمحاصيل.

segments.src: A breeder decides which two plants mate, then decides which of their offspring get to reproduce again.
segments.tr: يقرر المربي أي نباتين يتزاوجان، ثم يقرر أي من نسلهما يتكاثر مرة أخرى.

segments.src: Repeat for a decade or two, and you have a new variety — what farmers call a *cultivar*.
segments.tr: كرر لمدة عقد أو عقدين، وستحصل على صنف جديد — ما يسميه المزارعون *صنفاً*.

segments.src: There are two classic tools in the kit.
segments.tr: هناك أداتان كلاسيكيتان في المجموعة.

segments.src: **Selection breeding** is the older and simpler one.
segments.tr: **التربية الانتقائية** هي الأقدم والأبسط.

segments.src: You plant a field, walk through it, and keep seed only from the plants you like — the ones that resisted the blight, ripened early, or didn't fall over in a storm.
segments.tr: تزرع حقلاً، تمشي خلاله، وتحتفظ بالبذور فقط من النباتات التي تحبها — تلك التي تقاوم الآفة، نضجت مبكراً، أو لم تسقط في عاصفة.

segments.src: You're not creating anything new; you're concentrating the good genes that already exist in the population.
segments.tr: أنت لا تنشئ شيئاً جديداً؛ أنت تركز الجينات الجيدة التي تكون موجودة بالفعل في السكان.

segments.src: This is how humans turned a scraggly Mexican grass called teosinte into corn, one selective harvest at a time.
segments.tr: هذه هي الطريقة التي حول بها الإنسان عشباً مكسيكياً رقيقاً يسمى teosinte إلى الذرة، حصادة انتقائية في كل مرة.

segments.src: **Cross breeding (hybridization)** is more deliberate.
segments.tr: **التهجين (الهجانة)** أكثر تعمداً.

segments.src: You take two parents with different strengths — say, a wheat line with excellent bread-making quality and another that shrugs off stem rust — and physically move pollen from one to the other.
segments.tr: تأخذ والدين لهما نقاط قوة مختلفة — قل، صنفاً من القمح بجودة صنع خبز ممتازة وآخر يقاوم صدأ الساق — وتحرك فيزيائياً حبوب اللقاح من واحد إلى الآخر.

segments.src: The first generation of offspring is a genetic shuffle.
segments.tr: الجيل الأول من النسل هو خليط وراثي.

segments.src: Then the real work begins: growing out thousands of descendants and selecting, generation after generation, for the rare individual that inherited both traits at once.
segments.tr: ثم يبدأ العمل الحقيقي: تربية آلاف من الأحفاد واختيار، جيلاً بعد جيل، للفرد النادر الذي ورث كلا الصفتين في وقت واحد.

segments.src: Why so slow?
segments.tr: لماذا هذا بطيء جداً؟

segments.src: Because traits come bundled.
segments.tr: لأن الصفات تأتي معبأة معاً.
